audits.title: 396 A 6-Month Audit of Initial Diabetic Foot Assessment and Documentation for Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputations in An Orthopaedics Ward
audits.standard: ASEANPlus guidelines for diabetic foot wounds (foot inspection, vascular and neurological assessment)
audits.setting: Orthopaedics ward, Hospital Sultan Ismail, Johor Bahru; patients undergoing below- or above-knee amputation

cycle1.result: Foot inspection 100%; pulse palpation 94%; ABSI 76%; sensation 55%; ankle reflexes 25%.

audits.intervention: Suggested: teaching key examinations to junior staff and closer monitoring of documentation on ward rounds.
audits.other_findings: Only 67 of 81 records were available (AKA 26, BKA 41); poor practice attributed to lack of guidance for incoming junior doctors.
audits.citation: Lai L, Wong L, bin Hassan Z. 396 A 6-Month Audit of Initial Diabetic Foot Assessment and Documentation for Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputations in An Orthopaedics Ward. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.045.

audits.title: Improving diabetic foot screening at a primary care clinic: A quality improvement project.
audits.setting: Primary health care clinic, Western Cape
audits.intervention: Staff training on foot screening, patient information pamphlets and screening tools made available.
audits.other_findings: Health care workers' confidence in foot screening improved after training.
audits.citation: Allen ML, Van der Does AM, Gunst C. Improving diabetic foot screening at a primary care clinic: A quality improvement project. Afr J Prim Health Care Fam Med. 2016;8(1):e1-9. doi:10.4102/phcfm.v8i1.955. PMID: 27608673.

audits.title: 'CPR for Feet' care bundle to improve foot assessment in inpatient diabetes.
audits.standard: 'CPR for Feet' (Check, Protect and Refer) campaign guidelines
audits.setting: Glasgow Royal Infirmary inpatients with diabetes

cycle1.result: 28% had evidence of foot assessment; 13% of staff aware of the campaign

audits.intervention: Staff education and 'CPR for Feet' assessment checklist, then a 'CPR for Feet' care bundle after staff feedback (four PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: 72% had feet assessed and managed correctly; all staff aware of the campaign

audits.citation: O'Regan R, MacDonald R, Boyle JG, Hughes KA, McKenzie J. 'CPR for Feet' care bundle to improve foot assessment in inpatient diabetes. BMJ Open Qual. 2018;7(3):e000196. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000196. PMID: 30234169.

audits.title: Increasing identification of foot at risk of complications in patients with diabetes: a quality improvement project in an urban primary health centre in India.
audits.standard: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Diabetic Foot Guideline quality standard: annual foot assessment; aim 100% compliance within 6 months
audits.setting: Urban primary health centre, Mumbai (BARC Hospital)

cycle1.result: No patient with diabetes (0%) was offered preventive foot assessment.

audits.intervention: Standardised electronic medical record, training of health providers, redesigned clinic processes and referral pathways, weekly data review with PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 88.2% (848) of patients with diabetes received a foot examination; 11% (95) identified as foot at risk and referred.

audits.other_findings: 57% of referred patients attended specialist foot protection services; limited doctor time was the biggest barrier.
audits.citation: Mehndiratta A, Mishra SC, Bhandarkar P, Chhatbar K, Cluzeau F, PrimaryCareDoctors T. Increasing identification of foot at risk of complications in patients with diabetes: a quality improvement project in an urban primary health centre in India. BMJ Open Qual. 2020;9(3):e000893. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2019-000893. PMID: 32764027.

audits.title: Improving Early Identification and Documentation of High-Risk Diabetic Foot Complications Through a Closed-Loop Clinical Audit at Almanagil Teaching Hospital.
audits.standard: Structured diabetic foot risk assessment and documentation

cycle1.result: Patient identifiers recorded in 22%-60%; neuropathy, PAD and infection assessed in 8%-18%; risk score 2%; follow-up documented 22%.

audits.intervention: Staff education and a standardised diabetic foot risk assessment and scoring tool

cycle2.result: Identifiers 100%; neuropathy 98%; PAD 96%; infection and skin integrity 94%; risk score 92%; follow-up 96%.

audits.citation: Abdulrahman EAM, Wedatalla MAE, Mohammed AAY, Alabbas B, Ahmed ZKA, Ahmed EAE, et al.. Improving Early Identification and Documentation of High-Risk Diabetic Foot Complications Through a Closed-Loop Clinical Audit at Almanagil Teaching Hospital. Cureus. 2026;18(4):e106403. doi:10.7759/cureus.106403. PMID: 42088796.

audits.title: A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Intervention to Enhance Diabetic Foot Risk Assessment Compliance at Atbara Teaching Hospital.
audits.standard: International guideline-recommended structured diabetic foot risk assessment components

cycle1.result: Neuropathy assessed 8 (16%), peripheral arterial disease 3 (6%), risk stratification 0 (0%).

audits.intervention: Standardised diabetic foot risk assessment checklist with staff orientation and workflow integration

cycle2.result: Neuropathy assessment, vascular assessment, risk score and follow-up planning each 50 (100%) (p<0.001).

audits.other_findings: File number recording fell from 45 (90%) to 28 (56%).
audits.citation: Gadora WAA, Abdalla E, Eltayeb M, Abakar SAA, Ibrahim HBA, Awad MSA, et al.. A Closed-Loop Quality Improvement Intervention to Enhance Diabetic Foot Risk Assessment Compliance at Atbara Teaching Hospital. Cureus. 2026;18(5):e110000. doi:10.7759/cureus.110000. PMID: 42388546.
